housing: Stafford borough is the county town of Stafford, the canal town of Stone, and a large rural area of villages and farmland between Cannock Chase and the Shropshire border. Homes range from Victorian terraces near Stafford's centre to large post-war estates and recent new-build developments, with Georgian and older cottages in Eccleshall and the villages. Private renting is a little below average; the barracks at Beaconside add demand for family lets. HMOs are licensed only under the national scheme.
checkinTips: Victorian terraces near Stafford town centre: record the back yard, rear gate, gutters and any damp in rear rooms and cellars.
Canal-side homes in Stone and Great Haywood: check for damp, condensation and mould in ground-floor rooms and photograph moorings or gardens that run to the towpath.
Homes near the River Sow and Trent: check ground floors and gardens for signs of past flooding.
Rural homes off the gas grid: record the oil tank and gauge level or LPG tank, and any septic tank or treatment plant cover.
New-build estates around Stafford and Stone: photograph snagging items, sealant, paintwork and the garden, and note any estate management charge areas.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems can contact Stafford Borough Council's Housing Standards team, which can inspect homes and take action against landlords.
